# Introduction

The OMA Browser organises its genomes in a taxonomy derived from the NCBI
taxonomy. The taxonomic levels of this tree are the levels at which
Hierarchical Orthologous Groups and ancestral genomes are defined. This
vignette shows how to retrieve the taxonomy with `OmaDB` and how to use it
with the `r CRANpkg("ape")` package. See the vignette "Get started with
OmaDB" for an introduction to the package.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("OmaDB")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(OmaDB)
```

# Retrieving the taxonomy

`getTaxonomy()` returns the taxonomy in newick format. It can be
restricted to a subtree with the argument `root`, or to the taxonomy
induced by a set of genomes or taxonomic levels with `members`:

```{r taxonomy}
taxonomy <- getTaxonomy(members = c("YEAST", "ASHGO", "SCHPO", "HUMAN",
    "MOUSE", "DROME", "ARATH"))
taxonomy$root_taxon
taxonomy$newick
```

With `newick = FALSE`, the taxonomy is returned as a nested structure that
includes the NCBI taxon ids of all levels:

```{r dictionary}
tax <- getTaxonomy(members = c("YEAST", "ASHGO", "SCHPO"), newick = FALSE)
tax$name
tax$children[, c("name", "id")]
```

# Working with the tree

`getTree()` converts the taxonomy into a `phylo` object of the
`r CRANpkg("ape")` package, which can be visualised and analysed with ape
or other packages such as `r Biocpkg("ggtree")`.

```{r tree, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
tree <- getTree(taxonomy)
tree
plot(tree, show.node.label = TRUE, cex = 0.7, no.margin = TRUE,
    x.lim = 12)
```

The internal node labels are the taxonomic levels that can be used in the
other functions of the package, e.g. to retrieve the ancestral genome at a
level with `getHOGs()`:

```{r levels}
tree$node.label
```
